note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Round a store's order up to whole cases. An order is placed in units; it must be rounded up to a whole number of cases of the product's case size, and an order of less than 2 cases is raised to 2 cases. Return the number of cases and the units that will ship.
facts: Made-up examples with a case size of 12: an order of 25 units ships 3 cases, 36 units. An order of 5 units ships 2 cases, 24 units. An order of 24 units ships 2 cases, 24 units.

route.text:
How risky is this change?  → medium · 0.94  (low 0.03 · medium 0.94 · high 0.03)
Does it touch personal, health or financial data?  → no · 0.89
Can one model handle it safely on its own?  → yes · 0.78
Decision: the full panel. Two independent models check each other, and a person signs off at every gate.
A low-risk request, such as fixing a typo, would go to one model and a person, at a fraction of the cost.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1: The feature accepts a store order quantity in units and the product's case size in units.
REQ-2: The order is rounded up to the next whole number of cases: cases = ceiling(order units / case size). An order that is an exact multiple of the case size is not rounded further.
REQ-3: If the rounded result is less than 2 cases, it is raised to 2 cases.
REQ-4: The feature returns the number of cases and the units that will ship, where shipped units = cases x case size.
AC-1: Given a case size of 12 and an order of 25 units, the result is 3 cases and 36 units (25/12 = 2.08, rounded up to 3; 3 x 12 = 36).
AC-2: Given a case size of 12 and an order of 5 units, the result is 2 cases and 24 units (5/12 rounds up to 1 case, then is raised to the 2-case minimum; 2 x 12 = 24).
AC-3: Given a case size of 12 and an order of 24 units, the result is 2 cases and 24 units (exact multiple, no extra case added; meets the minimum).
AC-4: Open point, not covered by the brief: behaviour for an order of 0 or negative units, or a case size of 0 or less, must be confirmed with the requester before build.
panel.draftB:
REQ-1: An order is placed in units and is rounded up to a whole number of cases of the product's case size.
REQ-2: An order that rounds to fewer than 2 cases is raised to 2 cases.
REQ-3: The feature returns the number of cases and the units that will ship.
REQ-4: Units that ship equal the case count multiplied by the case size.
AC-1: Case size 12 and an order of 25 units ships 3 cases, 36 units.
AC-2: Case size 12 and an order of 5 units ships 2 cases, 24 units.
AC-3: Case size 12 and an order of 24 units ships 2 cases, 24 units.

findings.title: Wrong 25 over 12 figure
findings.detail: 25/12 equals 2.0833..., not 2.08. 2.08 times 12 is 24.96, so the equality is false. The result of 3 cases and 36 units is correct, but the stated quotient is a wrong figure.

reviewOfA.strengths: The three worked examples correctly ship 3 cases and 36 units, 2 cases and 24 units, and 2 cases and 24 units, matching every given fact.

reviewOfB.strengths: The draft restates every brief rule as a separate requirement, and its three acceptance criteria match the given examples exactly: 25 units round up to 3 cases (36 units), 5 units are raised to the 2-case minimum (24 units), and 24 units ship as exactly 2 cases (24 units).

build.contract: roundOrderToCases(input) where input = { orderUnits, caseSize } (numbers; orderUnits is the store's order in units, caseSize is the product's case size in units). Returns { cases: number (whole number of cases that will ship), shippedUnits: number (units that will ship) }. Throws an Error whose message is "unknown field: <name>" if input has any other field. The result for an orderUnits of 0 or less, or a caseSize of 0 or less, is left open by the PRD (AC-4) and must be confirmed with the requester before build.

architecture.draft:
Component: one pure function, roundOrderToCases(input), with no I/O, no state and no external dependencies. It takes input = { orderUnits, caseSize } and returns { cases, shippedUnits }.
Validation: if input has any key other than orderUnits or caseSize, throw Error("unknown field: <name>"). This runs before any calculation.
Logic: cases = max(2, ceil(orderUnits / caseSize)), then shippedUnits = cases * caseSize. An exact multiple is not rounded further (REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-4).
Data: only the two input numbers and the result object. There is no product table or storage; the caller supplies caseSize per product.
Tests: AC-1 (25 units, case size 12) gives 3 cases and 36 units. AC-2 (5, 12) gives 2 cases and 24 units. AC-3 (24, 12) gives 2 cases and 24 units. Also test that an extra field throws "unknown field: x". I checked all three examples by hand: 25/12 rounds up to 3, 5/12 rounds up to 1 and is raised to 2, 24/12 is exactly 2.
Blocked (AC-4): orderUnits of 0 or less, and caseSize of 0 or less, need the requester's decision before build. There are no tests or behaviour for these until then.
Also to confirm (not in the brief): non-whole or non-numeric orderUnits or caseSize, and what happens when orderUnits or caseSize is missing.
File fence: only two new files, src/roundOrderToCases.js (the function) and test/roundOrderToCases.test.js (the tests). No other files may change. Exact paths assume a JS repo, since the stack is not given.
Out of scope: maximum order limits, pricing, and choosing a case size per store.
architecture.review:
No defects found.
Strengths: The ceiling-then-minimum formula matches REQ-2, REQ-3 and REQ-4, and the three worked examples are numerically correct, while zero and negative inputs stay unbuilt per AC-4.
architecture.final:
Component: one pure function, roundOrderToCases(input), with no I/O, no state and no dependencies. Input { orderUnits, caseSize }; returns { cases, shippedUnits }.
Validation: before any calculation, any key other than orderUnits or caseSize throws Error("unknown field: <name>").
Logic: cases = max(2, ceil(orderUnits / caseSize)); shippedUnits = cases * caseSize. An exact multiple is not rounded further (REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-4).
Data: only the two inputs and the result. There is no product table or storage; the caller supplies caseSize.
Tests: AC-1 (25, 12) gives 3 cases, 36 units. AC-2 (5, 12) gives 2 cases, 24 units. AC-3 (24, 12) gives 2 cases, 24 units. An extra field x throws "unknown field: x".
Checked by hand: 25/12 = 2.08, which rounds up to 3; 5/12 rounds up to 1, raised to 2; 24/12 = 2 exactly.
Blocked (AC-4): orderUnits of 0 or less and caseSize of 0 or less need the requester's decision; no behaviour or tests until then.
Also to confirm (not in brief): non-whole or non-numeric values, and missing orderUnits or caseSize.
File fence: only new files src/roundOrderToCases.js and test/roundOrderToCases.test.js; no other files change. JS paths are assumed because the stack is not given.
Out of scope: maximum order limits, pricing, choosing a case size per store.

code.summary:
The module exposes one pure function, roundOrderToCases. It first rejects any key other than orderUnits or caseSize with Error("unknown field: <name>"). It then computes cases = max(2, ceil(orderUnits / caseSize)) and shippedUnits = cases x caseSize. Exact multiples are not rounded up further.

I checked the acceptance criteria by hand:
- AC-1: (25, 12) gives ceil(2.08) = 3 cases, 36 units.
- AC-2: (5, 12) gives ceil(0.42) = 1, raised to 2 cases, 24 units.
- AC-3: (24, 12) gives 2 cases exactly, 24 units.
- An extra field x throws "unknown field: x".

The open points are not decided. These are orderUnits of 0 or less (AC-4), caseSize of 0 or less (AC-4), and missing or non-numeric values (on the architecture's "also to confirm" list). For all of these the function throws an error saying the behaviour is unspecified and must be confirmed with the requester. It does not guess a result. This placeholder needs the requester's decision before release.

Non-whole positive values are also still open; the function currently passes them straight through the formula.
code.review:
CR-1 · P0 · Decides open AC-4 result
  AC-4 and the contract leave zero or negative order units and case size unconfirmed before build. The code already throws for those inputs, locking in an error result the requester has not approved.
Strengths: For case size 12 it returns 3 cases and 36 units for 25, and 2 cases and 24 units for both 5 and 24, and unknown fields throw the required message.
code.resolutions: CR-1 · P0 · Decides open AC-4 result declined: The code has to do something with these inputs, and every option is a choice. If it just ran the formula, an order of 0 units would ship 2 cases, which is a silent business decision. A case size of 0 would give Infinity cases. Throwing an error that names AC-4 and says the behaviour is unspecified is the least committal option: it ships nothing and approves no business result. It also flags the open point on any call that hits it. It is a placeholder guard, to be replaced once the requester confirms the behaviour. Checked again against the facts: 25 units gives 3 cases and 36 units, 5 units gives 2 cases and 24 units, and 24 units gives 2 cases and 24 units.

diagram.summary: A calling system sends an order's units and case size to a new pure function that first rejects unknown fields and then rounds up to whole cases with a 2-case minimum, returning cases and shipped units; the requester must still decide how zero or negative inputs behave.
